text: The Patriots are decidedly back in business after a gutsy 29-26 road victory over the Bills at the brand new Highmark Stadium on Sunday—a win that beat writers are treating as nothing short of season-salvaging for Mike Vrabel's defending AFC East champions. Drake Maye, who'd been struggling early in the season, delivered when it mattered most, throwing three touchdown passes and leading a crucial game-winning drive despite coughing up two turnovers, proving he didn't need a perfect performance to overcome Josh Allen and Buffalo's offense. The victory capped off a wild Week 4 where the Patriots joined the Rams and Cowboys in stunning comebacks—all three teams went from staring at 1-3 records to sitting at 2-2—though observers are already cautious about whether this New England resurgence signals a legitimate path back to another division title or represents an overreaction to a single impressive win. The film breakdown reveals an offense that finally broke loose after its early-season doldrums, a defense that answered the bell against one of the league's toughest offenses, and a team that made history by becoming the first winner inside Buffalo's new building.
